text:
maya: Heads up — kicking off a needlepoint canary for the routing service. shifting 1% of prod -> v2026.3 now. please watch latency/5xx for 10m. deploy-bot will post rollout events. :eyes:

deploy-bot: [automated] rollout started: service=routing tag=v2026.3 percent=1 user=maya window=change-window-10-12UTC

alex: noted. rollback criteria? we should be explicit: >=.5% 5xx or p99 > 400ms for 3m => rollback.

maya: agreed on rollback triggers. add KV-cache OOMs to the list (if any).

ryan: change window confirmed 10-12UTC. release notes updated in the docs link: https://docs.internal/release-notes/2026.3

lina: quick check — throwing up a tracing link, will watch tail for errors: https://telemetry/routing/v2026.3/stream :chart_with_upwards_trend:

alex: also recommend pinning older model variant to 0% -> keep available for instant fallback. deploy-bot can pin via API.

maya: good call. deploy-bot, please stage a pinned fallback: v2026.2-stable at 100% standby.

deploy-bot: executed: create-fallback service=routing fallback=v2026.2-stable status=ready

lina: seeing a tiny p95 bump at 90s into canary (p95 +12ms) — no 5xx yet. continuing to observe.

ryan: can we get traces for the requests that hit kv cache? I want sample ids.

lina: grabbing samples, posting below.

lina: ```
trace_id: 0a1b2c3d sample=3 route=/generate seq=128 kv_miss=true p99=412ms
trace_id: 0a1b2c3e sample=7 route=/generate seq=64 kv_miss=false p99=198ms
```

alex: okay those traces show a coupling with kv_miss and higher tail. if we see sustained p99 > 400ms for 3 consecutive minutes, we should hold at current percent and run diag.

maya: consensus? Recommend holding at 1% until 10:20UTC for one more observation window. If clear, go to 3% then.

ryan: +1 for hold. I'll open an infra ticket to check cache eviction thresholds in the canary pool.

deploy-bot: [automated] percent update: currently=1 target=1

lina: at 10:12UTC another spike but only for kv_miss traces. no 5xx. p99 peaks at 430ms for a handful of requests.

alex: hmm borderline. Do we have a quick mitigant? maybe reduce sequence length defaults for canary traffic or enable prefix-cache for those routes.

maya: can't change model code mid-rollout. Can we route shorter sequence traffic off the canary? not ideal.

ryan: creating temporary route filter to route requests with seq>256 to fallback cluster for now. will push in 2m.

lina: capturing increased error budget risk in ops dashboard.

maya: decision: hold at 1%, action items: (1) ryan to push route filter, (2) lina to keep telemetry live, (3) alex to prepare rollback playbook if 5xx triggers, (4) maya to call go/no-go at 10:20UTC.

alex: noted. prep rollback steps and smoke tests now.

ryan: route filter applied: filter=seq>256 -> fallback cluster. deploy-bot: confirm?

deploy-bot: executed: route-update service=routing filter="seq>256" action=redirect fallback=v2026.2-stable

lina: after filter, tail looks stable. p99 back to ~210ms, no 5xx.

maya: thanks. we'll reconvene at 10:20UTC for go to 3% or roll forward depending on telemetry. :thumbsup:

alex: +1

ryan: +1

deploy-bot: [automated] thread note: to escalate, tag @oncall.

maya: ending interim check — will post final decision at 10:20UTC.
